title: Space stations, telemetry and telecommand
blurb: Tell telemetry from telecommand, know who may run space-link stations, and which bands carry space stations.

E1D01.why: Telemetry is a **one-way transmission of measurements** taken at a distance from the instrument.

E1D02.why: Only **telecommand signals from a space telecommand station** may be encrypted. Terrestrial links, relays and mesh nodes may not.

E1D03.why: A space telecommand station **sends commands** that initiate, modify or terminate a space station's functions.
E1D03.trap: Receiving telemetry or sitting above 50 km describes other stations.

E1D04.why: A balloon telemetry station's ID must include its **call sign**. Power and grid are not required.

E1D05.why: A telecommand station on or within 50 km of the surface must post **all three**: a license copy, the licensee label and the control operator label.

E1D06.why: A model craft telecommand transmitter is limited to **1 watt**.

E1D07.why: On HF, space stations have allocations on **40, 20, 15 and 10 m**. Not 30 or 17 m.

E1D08.why: Of the VHF bands only **2 m** has space station frequencies. Not 6 m or 1.25 m.

E1D09.why: On UHF, space stations may use **70 cm and 13 cm**. Not 33 cm.

E1D10.why: The **space station licensee** designates which stations may be telecommand stations. AMSAT and the ITU do not.

E1D11.why: **Any** amateur station may be an Earth station, within its control operator's license privileges. No course or class needed.

E1D12.why: One-way communications are allowed for a **space station, beacon station or telecommand station**. Repeaters and forwarding stations are two-way.
